questions.question: What type of algorithm is Merge Sort?
questions.explanation: Merge Sort is a classic example of a Divide and Conquer algorithm.

questions.question: What is the time complexity of Merge Sort in the worst case?
questions.explanation: Merge Sort has a time complexity of O(n log n) in all cases (worst, average, and best).

questions.question: What is a prerequisite for Binary Search?

options.text: The list must contain only unique elements
The list must be of a certain size

questions.explanation: Binary search requires the array or list to be sorted to work correctly.

questions.question: What is the time complexity of Binary Search?
questions.explanation: Due to its divide-and-conquer nature, binary search has a logarithmic time complexity.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a type of linked list?
questions.explanation: Singly, Doubly, and Circular are all standard types of linked lists. Sequential is not a standard term.

questions.question: What is a collision in a hash table?

options.text: Two keys having the same value
Two keys hashing to the same index
Two different hash tables storing the same key
A key that is not found in the table

questions.explanation: A collision occurs when the hash function generates the same index for more than one key.

questions.question: What data structure is typically used to implement BFS?
questions.explanation: BFS uses a queue to store the nodes to visit, ensuring that nodes are explored level by level.

questions.question: What data structure is typically used to implement DFS?
questions.explanation: DFS uses a stack (often the call stack via recursion) to explore as far as possible down one branch before backtracking.
